concerns.text: The plan treats low‑level visual features (luminance, contrast, edge density) as *diagnostic only* and excludes them from the final mixed‑effects model (FR‑009 – diagnostic only), while the research specification (research.md) explicitly requires these features to be included as covariates to control for confounding (see FR‑009 in the spec). Because salience maps are themselves computed from low‑level image properties, omitting these covariates makes the predictor (salience_score) mathematically linked to the outcome (attention) through shared low‑level features. This creates a definitional/tautological relationship that the analysis will inevitably confirm, undermining the scientific claim that salience *independently* predicts attentional allocation.
